EXTRA CLASS · SEQUENCE STORIES · 24 CARDS · AGES 3–5

Sequence story flashcards — 24 little stories to put in the right order.

Twenty-four printable sequencing cards for ages three to five: one little story told in four labeled pictures on every card — bedtime, building a snowman, making toast. Cut them out, mix them up, put the story back in order and tell it out loud. Every card below prints free, downloads full size and carries one plain tip on how to run it tonight — the whole class lives on this single page.

More extra classes ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Cut the pictures. Mix them up. Put the story back.

Print a card, cut along the four squares, shuffle them face up, and hand the pile over: “Put the story in order.” Your child lays out first, next, then, last — those four words are the whole lesson, and they are pre-reading in disguise. Once the order is built, the retelling matters more than the right answer: “Tell me the story with your pictures.” Wrong orders are welcome too — spotting that the boots came after the puddle is thinking, not failing.

One card a day is plenty, and the stories do the motivating: they are things your child already does — washing hands, tidying toys, eating toast. Two cards happen in the kitchen, make-toast and make-lemonade, and they carry an Ask a grown-up badge: hot and slippery jobs belong to grown-ups, the child runs the story. The badge prints with the card, so it travels to the fridge too.

THE CARDS · 24 STORIES

Every story, its tip, and the button to print it.

Each tile is the card itself: the artwork prints at full size with the Download button, and Print runs just that one card through your printer. The tip under each card is the whole lesson — one way to set the ordering talk up tonight.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the ordering grows next.

Put the story in order after Class 29 · Ages 4–5 ↗Order games in Class 30 · Ages 4–5 ↗Routines in Class 32 · Ages 4–5 ↗All the extra classes ↗

Class 29 reads real stories and asks who, what and what-next; Class 30 turns ordering into patterns, mazes and secret codes; and Class 32 grows the same routines this deck tells in pictures — washing hands, tidying up, setting the table. Print a story after storytime, and the sequencing quietly becomes reading readiness.

First, next, then, last. Four little words, and every story your child meets for the rest of school hangs on them — the cards just make the words something small hands can hold.

STORY ORDER, DAY ORDER

Class 41 · Time & Daily Routine.

Sequence Stories puts four-picture stories in order — first, next, last — and the Time & Daily Routine class runs the same order words across a whole day: the morning’s five steps, the afternoon’s lunch-learn-play-snack, the evening’s tidy-dinner-teeth-pajamas-sleep. Forty-one printable time cards for ages 4–5 with the rule on every card and one way to try it today — the sequencing practice your family just did with stories, now on your child’s own routine.
